name: Sloppity Bilepiper
oracle_text: Jolly Gutpipes — {2}, {T}, Sacrifice a creature: The next creature spell you cast this turn has cascade. (When you next cast a creature spell, exile cards from the top of your library until you exile a nonland card that costs less. You may cast it without paying its mana cost. Put the exiled cards on the bottom in a random order.)
blocked_sentences: Jolly Gutpipes — {2}, {T}, Sacrifice a creature: The next creature spell you cast this turn has cascade.

needs.what: an effect that gives the next spell matching a filter (here: a creature spell) that a player (here: you) casts this turn the cascade ability itself, so the spell HAS cascade (seen by 'whenever you cast a spell with cascade' triggers), its cascade trigger's source is that spell, the ceiling is that spell's mana value, and the grant is used up by that one spell and expires at end of turn
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `cascade` is not in `keywords`, so `grant_keyword`/`cast_gains_keywords` cannot hand it to a spell, and `next_spell_cost_reduction`/`grant_flash_permission`/`uncounterable_this_turn` are the only next-spell grants and none carries a keyword or ability. The nearest arrangement, a `delayed_trigger` (duration once_this_turn) on `spell_cast` with a Creature filter running the `cascade` op with max_mana_value from the subject, is an approximation: the trigger belongs to the Bilepiper rather than the spell, the spell never has cascade (so The First Doctor-style 'spell with cascade' checks miss it), and op_cascade's default ceiling is the source permanent's mana value. The activation cost ({2}, {T}, sacrifice a creature) is expressible.
